summary: Nan is the warlord's realm of islands and peninsulas: Dumar of Vez Nan and his captains, the storm wayfinders, the tales of the Stair, wayfinders for Nafeher, the wardens or no one, and isles that endure the war.

one_warlord_spirit.name: One Warlord
one_warlord_spirit.desc: Dumar of Vez Nan speaks for all the isles, and the captains obey because he speaks seldom and is seldom wrong. A single voice is a hard thing to argue with in a gale.

captains_moot.name: The Captains' Moot
captains_moot.desc: The captains of the isles meet on the deck of a beached hulk and argue from dawn until the tide turns. What they decide at the turn, they do.

nan_and_vez_nan_spirit.name: Nan and Vez Nan
nan_and_vez_nan_spirit.desc: The islands of Nan and the hills of Vez Nan are one realm, bound by marriage, sea-roads and a common dislike of outsiders. Where one is struck, the other bleeds.

storm_pilots_spirit.name: The Storm Wayfinders
storm_pilots_spirit.desc: The wayfinders of Nan know the reefs, the currents and the moods of the storm belt as other folk know their own street. Foreign fleets founder where Nan's hulls sail through.

storm_wall.name: The Storm Is Our Wall
storm_wall.desc: Nan's coast is guarded by the storm itself, and by bunkers that make use of it. An enemy that tries to land must first survive the weather, and then the defenders.

rim_watch.name: Watchers on the Rim
rim_watch.desc: Watchers sit on the inland rim of Vez Nan, looking down into the dark and listening. They have seen nothing come up the Stair in living memory, and they mean to keep it so.

own_storms.name: Wayfinders for No One
own_storms.desc: Nan's wayfinders serve no fleet but their own, and they sail their storms for Nan alone. Visitors are welcome to look at the sea from the shore.

warlords_host.name: The Warlord's Host
warlords_host.desc: The warbands of the isles and the peninsulas are drawn into a single host under the warlord's banner. It is loud, ragged and surprisingly well-fed.

storm_shelter.name: The Storm Shelters Us
storm_shelter.desc: The storm closes in around the isles like a hand. An enemy fleet sailing toward Nan must pass through it, and Nan's own hulls do not.

pilots_of_nafeher.name: Wayfinders of Nan
pilots_of_nafeher.desc: Wayfinders of Nan guide Nafeher's hulls through the storm belt, for a fee and a promise of silence. The fleet that follows them sails faster and lands sooner.

warlord_speaks.title: The Warlord Speaks
warlord_speaks.desc: The longhouse is full, and the fire is built high. Dumar of Vez Nan stands, folds his arms and tells the gathered captains and island lords what he expects of them.

tales_of_the_stair.title: Tales of the Stair
tales_of_the_stair.desc: Inland of Vez Nan a stair goes down into the dark. Long ago a stranger from the north went down it and came back up. The elders do not say what he carried, and no one in Nan has gone to look.

nan_offers_pilots.title: Wayfinders from Nan
nan_offers_pilots.desc: A boat from the isles has come to the coast of the Dominion, carrying a master wayfinder and a modest request. Nan offers its wayfinders to Nafeher's fleet, for a fee and a promise to be left alone.

ships_for_the_exiles.title: Ships for the Exiles
ships_for_the_exiles.desc: Black hulls come out of the storm at dusk, with lamps hooded and oars muffled. The wayfinders of Nan have kept their promise, and the exiles of Mirolon go aboard in silence.

an_answer_from_the_isles.title: An Answer from the Isles
an_answer_from_the_isles.desc: A boat from Nan comes in on the tide with a message from the warlord. The offer has been taken, and Dumar sends his thanks, which are brief.

nan_pilots_for_the_wardens.title: Wayfinders for the Wardens
nan_pilots_for_the_wardens.desc: Envoys from the isles stand in the lake-hall of Mirolon and offer the wardens their wayfinders, to carry the free south's exiles if the worst comes. Dumar's price is a handshake and a promise of silence.

the_offer_refused.title: The Offer Refused
the_offer_refused.desc: The envoys come back with nothing, and a bad grace. Dumar listens to the report, shrugs and says that the storm needs no allies.

focuses.name: The Warlord of Vez Nan
focuses.desc: Warlord Dumar holds the hills of Vez Nan and the islands of Nan with a few thousand spears and a very good memory for faces. His hall is a longhouse of black timber on a rise above the sea.

focuses.name: Dumar's Captains
focuses.desc: Dumar keeps a dozen captains who have each sailed for him a lifetime. They meet over a map scratched in the floor and argue about the reefs.

focuses.name: The Island Lords
focuses.desc: The lords of the outer isles come to the warlord's hall once a year, each in his own boat. They swear to the warlord, drink his ale and sail home before the weather turns.

focuses.name: One Warlord
focuses.desc: The captains and the lords agree that there shall be one warlord and one will. Dumar takes the seat in the stern, and nobody argues with the man at the tiller.

focuses.name: The Captains' Moot
focuses.desc: The captains persuade Dumar that a moot of the fleet is wiser than a single will, and he agrees. They meet on the deck of a beached hulk and argue from dawn until the tide turns.

focuses.name: Nan and Vez Nan
focuses.desc: Nan and Vez Nan are declared one realm, with one banner and one law. The islands send fish and sailors, and the hills send iron and spears.

focuses.name: The Storm Wayfinders
focuses.desc: Nan's sailors know the reefs and the storm belt of the Ember Lands' coast, where foreign fleets founder and no other men sail for a living. The master wayfinder Seska runs the school that teaches the young to read the waves.

focuses.name: The Black Reefs Charted
focuses.desc: Every reef and shoal is charted by the wayfinders, and the charts are cut in slate and kept in the warlord's strongroom. A fleet that has them can sail the coast blind, and a fleet that has not will run aground.

focuses.name: The Harbour of Nan
focuses.desc: A deep harbour is cut into the rock of the main island, with a mole against the swell and a chain across the mouth. Its dockyard rings with caulking-mallets.

focuses.name: The Storm Is Our Wall
focuses.desc: Nan's captains say that the storm is their wall, and set bunkers on the beaches that make the most of it. A fleet that crosses the belt arrives weakened, and meets a defender who is waiting.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for Hire
focuses.desc: Wayfinders are hired out to foreign merchants for a season, and come home with silver and stories. The warlord takes a tenth, and asks nothing about the stories.

focuses.name: Tales of the Stair
focuses.desc: Inland of Vez Nan, the elders say, a stair goes down into the dark. Long ago a stranger from the north went down it and came back up, and the tale is told at the warlord's fire.

focuses.name: Watchers on the Rim
focuses.desc: Watchers are posted on the inland rim, in huts of piled stone, each with a horn and a store of firewood. Nothing has come up the Stair in living memory, but the watch goes on.

focuses.name: Leave the Deep Alone
focuses.desc: The elders agree that what lies below should be left alone. The Stair is fenced, the paths to it are closed and the children are taught to keep away.

focuses.name: What the Deep Keeps
focuses.desc: The elders say that the Abyss-folk keep to their dark, and Nan keeps to its sea. Neither disturbs the other, and both are content.

focuses.name: Between Storm and Sea
focuses.desc: Nafeher in the south and Mirolon in the north both want Nan's wayfinders. Dumar listens to both and gives neither a firm answer.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for Nafeher
focuses.desc: Nafeher would pay well for wayfinders who can steer a fleet through the storm belt. Dumar considers the offer, and the coin, and the silence that would follow.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for the Wardens
focuses.desc: Mirolon's wardens ask for wayfinders to carry their exiles north if the passes fall. Dumar does not refuse, and does not promise.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for No One
focuses.desc: Dumar decides that Nan's wayfinders will serve no fleet but their own. The storm belongs to Nan, and Nan is not for hire to the great.

focuses.name: Dark Coin
focuses.desc: The coin from Nafeher is black glass, stamped with a horned head. It spends well in the free ports, and no one asks where it came from.

focuses.name: The Exiles' Road
focuses.desc: Nan's wayfinders carry Mirolon's exiles north on moonless nights, through the storm belt and out of reach of Nafeher. The warlord is paid in gratitude, which he accepts.

focuses.name: The Warlord's Neutrality
focuses.desc: Dumar announces that the isles are neutral and will remain so. The announcement is read in every harbour, and is received without surprise.

focuses.name: Island Warbands
focuses.desc: Each island and each peninsula raises its own warband, led by a captain of its own, with its own banner and its own battle-cry. They are rough, ready and fond of ambushes.

focuses.name: Reef Raiders
focuses.desc: Light boats run between the reefs with crews of ten, who board a becalmed merchantman and are gone before the wind returns. They are the isles' answer to a fleet.

focuses.name: Peninsula Forts
focuses.desc: Stone forts are raised at the neck of every peninsula, with a gate that can be shut in a breath. A host that lands on Nan must take them one by one.

focuses.name: The Warlord's Host
focuses.desc: The warbands are drawn into a single host under the warlord's banner. It is loud, ragged and surprisingly well-fed.

focuses.name: The Isles at War
focuses.desc: The signal-fires burn on every headland, and the warlord's horn is heard across the strait. The isles are at war, and Dumar has not been so cheerful in years.

focuses.name: The Storm Shelters Us
focuses.desc: The storm closes in around the isles like a hand. An enemy fleet sailing toward Nan must pass through it, and Nan's own hulls do not.

focuses.name: Raiders of the Reefs
focuses.desc: Reef raiders slip out of the shallows by night and take whatever they find. The enemy never sees them coming, and never sees them go.

focuses.name: The Isles Endure
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the isles are still isles. The storm is still the wall, and the wayfinders put out to sea again.
